title: How to Start Giving Generously
excerpt: Generosity is not a feeling you wait for. It is a practice that produces the feeling. Here is how to begin, with a real number, this month, before you feel ready.
body:
Nobody starts giving generously by feeling generous first. We wait for a flush of warmth, a season of abundance, a moment when it finally feels safe to open the hand. That moment does not come. The bank account is never quite full enough, the future never quite secure enough, and so the giving keeps getting postponed to a tomorrow that stays one paycheck away.

Generosity is not a feeling you act on. It is an action that, over time, produces the feeling. You give your way into a generous heart. You do not feel your way into a generous gift.

## Understand what you are fighting

Jesus called money by a name, Mammon, as if it were a rival god. He did this on purpose. "You cannot serve God and money" is not advice about budgeting. It is a warning that money wants your worship, and it competes for the throne.

Generosity is the weapon against that god. Every gift you give is a small act of treason against Mammon, a way of saying with your hands that this money does not own you. That is why giving feels like loss before it feels like freedom. You are prying your fingers off something they have been gripping a long time.

I have felt that grip. I have done the math on a gift and felt actual fear, as if the dollars leaving were a piece of my safety walking out the door. That fear is the most honest evidence I have that I needed to give.

## Start with a number, not an intention

"I want to be more generous" is not a plan. It is a wish, and wishes do not move money. Pick a number and a date.

Do not start with the number that sounds impressive. Start with the number you can actually move this month without it being a fantasy. For some that is the biblical tithe, ten percent. For someone deep in debt and barely making rent, it might be twenty dollars. The amount matters less than the fact that it is real, recurring, and decided in advance.

The early church was not measured by the size of the gift. The widow put in two small coins and Jesus said she gave more than all the wealthy, because they gave from abundance and she gave from her need. He was not impressed by the total. He was watching the cost.

## Give off the top, automatically

Willpower is a terrible giving strategy. If generosity depends on you feeling moved at the end of the month, it will lose every time to the things that already have your attention.

So automate it, or at least move it first. The day your income arrives, the gift goes out, before the bills, before the budget, before life lays its claims. The firstfruits pattern in Scripture is not arbitrary. Giving first does something to you that giving last cannot. It puts God ahead of your fear, every cycle, on a schedule your feelings do not get to veto.

## Give to faces, not just causes

Write the check to your church, yes. But also keep some giving close enough to touch. The single mother in your row at church. The family three doors down. The friend whose car died and who has not told anyone.

This matters because distant giving can become abstract, a transaction that never reaches your heart. When you hand money to a person whose relief you can see, generosity stops being a budget line and becomes love with a face attached. That is the kind that changes you.

## Let it grow, and watch your heart follow

Start real and small, then raise it. Add a percent. Add a name. The goal is not a fixed tax you pay forever but a hand that slowly opens wider over a lifetime.

And watch what happens inside you. Jesus promised that where your treasure goes, your heart follows. Send treasure toward the kingdom, toward the poor, toward your church, and you will find, slowly, that you begin to care about the things your money is already serving. The giving leads. The heart catches up. This is the order Jesus gave us, and it works in exactly that direction.

## This week

Choose one number and one recipient. Set it to recur, or move it manually the moment your next pay arrives, off the top, before anything else. Then notice the fear, if it comes, and do not let it talk you out of the gift. The fear is not a reason to stop. It is the proof that you have found the thing that owned you, and that you have, for once, refused it.
